params.reason: record why the hooks were paused (default: manual)

#/answers: paused (exit 0)  the marker stands; a capture hook steps aside until resumed
#/gate: write: a marker file in the house's own run space; reversible by resume, trusted
#/head: capture minting stops at the source

The hook-lever stands on its own: a marker file a capture hook checks and steps aside on when present (whatever runs the `lares sense capture` and `lares sense telemetry` legs on a session event). A migration or a `lares sense teardown` then runs WITHOUT daemon-spawn contention: the minting stops at the source, with no whack-a-mole against spawned children. `lares mempalace quiesce` pauses AND drains the warm daemons in one gesture; this lever suppresses minting alone, touching no live daemon.

`hooks pause [--reason <t>]` writes the marker (the reason defaults to `manual`) and answers {wasPaused, hooksPaused, marker, since, reason}; pausing again refreshes the reason. Run `lares mempalace quiesce` to drain the warm daemons, and `hooks resume` to un-pause.

Already-landed turns skip, so a re-run catches up. `bulk` reads no `pointer`, `room`, `dry-run` or `writeback`: each refuses by name beside it, since the sweep previews nothing. `sensorium` names the sensorium; absent, memory.

The address stands ''candidate'' until the operator reads the landing's list. `lares sense search <query…>` runs hybrid recall over one plane (`--lens`, default content; `crossplane` widens content hits across form and structure by the cid join), `--k` hits (default 5), narrowed by `--wing` and `--room`. `--not-root` (else `LARES_SESSION_ROOT`) down-weights the caller's own session by `--self-weight` (default 0.25). A frozen trial (`--trial-root`, with `--model-home` for the pinned query model) reads its owned Content and frontiers, filtered to its receipts, `--source-key` and `--revision` narrowing it. A leading sensorium name (`lares sense <sensorium> <verb>`) addresses any named sensorium; bare, the verb reads `memory`.
#/refuses: usage  no verb or no query named
cure: lares sense search harbor
verb-error  an unknown lens, a trial flag without --trial-root, a trial with no --model-home, or the read failed

lares sense search harbor --lens structure --k 10    # ten hits over the structure plane

The low-level instruments (crystallize · phase · whiten · couple · gate · mismatch) stand as building blocks a FLOW composes, never the surface: the flow set (crystal · rhythm · couple) carries each pet name, its arity and its cap-stack. Bare `flow` LISTS the set with each cap-stack, in process with no daemon (the seeds ship in the mesh package). A pet name with a `signal` matrix (rows = time, columns = signals; `names` labels the columns) RUNS that flow: the daemon looks its cap-stack up and runs each step routed by hull (crystallize and couple in TypeScript, phase in Python, mismatch in the daemon), threading each outcome to the next. New capability arrives as a new flow.

The CLI reads the signal from an NDJSON file, one JSON array per non-blank line; the seat hands the rows. `target` names the sensorium streams a run reads as provenance: a target with no signal asks the projector to extract one from the target's child streams, which stands feature-gated (the projector runs now, empty until the re-pour lands child signals), so auto-extraction from a poured target stays OWED.

#/gate: seat: the vessel verbs the seat's handler reaches check the face's cap and the asker's hand themselves; a hand act refuses a seat by its own code
#/head: run one analysis lens

`lens` chooses the instrument: changes, rhythm, couple (house name ki), cohere (house name li), square, lead, forecast, mismatch. The first five read the poured sensorium; lead, forecast and mismatch read the `rows` matrix the caller hands in (`names` labels its columns) and touch no plane. A missing or unknown lens refuses naming every lens, and an argument the lens reads none of refuses by name.
On the terminal the matrix rides `--signal <ndjson>`; each lens reads its own flags:
changes    where the poured content changes hands (--spectral, --halves <w,w>, --span <n>)

ddate.brief: read the Discordian date from the house's own calendar; no vessel
help: usage: lares ddate [+FORMAT] [<day> <month> <year>]
lares ddate — read the Discordian date from the house's own calendar; no vessel
the day in the Discordian calendar, from the house's own core

The house computes the day in the Discordian calendar with its own isomorphic core, so a machine with no host `ddate` binary (a vessel's container, a bare host) reads it all the same. Five seasons of 73 days (Chaos, Discord, Confusion, Bureaucracy, The Aftermath) run a five-day week (Sweetmorn, Boomtime, Pungenday, Prickle-Prickle, Setting Orange); the YOLD runs the Gregorian year plus 1166; St. Tib's Day falls on February 29 with no season and no weekday; an apostle's holyday falls on day 5 of a season and its season holyday on day 50.

With no date the verb reads today's local day: the command and the seat each read the clock once, at the caller's side of the seam, and hand the day to the core, which reads none. The `day`, `month` and `year` ride together or not at all (a BCE year rides negative), and a date out of range refuses. X-Day (Confusion 40, 9827 YOLD) stands as the Church of the SubGenius's date, moved forward once the first X-Day passed without incident; `%X` counts the days to it.

Format codes follow ddate(1), with `%E` added: `%A %a` weekday, long and short · `%B %b` season, long and short · `%d` day of the season · `%e` the ordinal (1st, 11th, 21st, 22nd, 23rd) · `%E` the ordinal by its last digit alone (11st, 12nd, 13rd), the first ddate's reading, an easter egg · `%H` the day's holyday, if any · `%N` stop here unless the day holds a holyday · `%Y` the YOLD · `%X` days until X-Day (negative once it passed) · `%n %t` newline, tab · `%.` an exclamation from the platform's entropy door (crypto.getRandomValues) · `%{ %}` the span between them reads "St. Tib's Day" on February 29 and prints plain on every other day.

A bare call answers the default line ("Today is Prickle-Prickle, the 32nd day of The Aftermath in the YOLD 3192"). On a terminal that line prints plain, like ddate(1), and `--json` answers the envelope the seat always returns: {text, entropy, gregorian, yold, tibs, season, dayOfSeason, weekday, holyday}, where `entropy` names the source a `%.` drew from, else null. The verb runs on the host and needs no vessel; the MCP tool rides the @daemon wire.
Examples:
lares ddate    # today, with the default format
lares ddate 5 1 2024    # a named day: Setting Orange, Chaos 5, 3190 YOLD
lares ddate '+%{%A, the %e of %B%}, %Y. %N%nCelebrate %H' 19 2 2025    # a format over a named day, the holyday line only on a holyday
lares ddate '+%X' 20 11 2026    # days until X-Day
lares ddate '+%. %E'    # an exclamation and the first ddate's ordinal

+FORMAT  the ddate(1) format codes the head lists; absent, the default line
<day>  the day of the month; day, month and year ride together or not at all
<month>  the month, 1 to 12; rides with day and year
<year>  the Gregorian year (a BCE year rides negative); rides with day and month

clock: the caller names the day: with no date the command or the seat reads its own local calendar day once and hands it to the core, which reads no clock

delete.brief: remove one record, or a meme family by name, from a wiki or bag
help: usage: lares delete [mu=<carry>] title=<title> [base=<hash>] [family=<true>] [way=<kapae-or-reveal>] (recipe=<slug> | bag=<slug>) [realm=<id>] [face=<handle>] [mu=<carry>]
lares delete — remove one record, or a meme family by name, from a wiki or bag
a delete by the family law, plain unless a lower layer makes it a choice

A delete deletes plainly: with no `way`, each record leaves its own layer to absent and no tombstone rises (the receipt reads `mode: "plain"` and names each title under `retracted`). `base` carries the hash last read: a record that moved past it moves nothing and answers `conflict`, naming the live hash. A title the wiki reads absent answers `absent`, and a plain delete there retracts a kāpae that hides nothing (its `.kapae` shadow leaves the disk). The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

The family law decides what moves, read over the reader's view before anything lands. A plain tiddler leaves alone. A meme root answers the consequence the delete would land (every title it would move, what it would leave) and refuses `tiddler-delete-in-a-family` unless `family` names the family act, which lands the root and its slots as one change per layer (the answer adds `canonicalHash`). A slot's title (`<root>#/x`) leaves as the explicit cut on its parent, and the family reseals.

Only a lower layer makes a delete a choice. A wiki composes layers (canon under working under personal), and one title may stand in several. Where a lower layer holds the title too, or the record rests in a layer this face cannot remove it from, a delete naming no way refuses `delete-mode-needed` and names both meanings: `way=kapae` raises a tombstone in a writable layer that shadows every record beneath (the wiki reads the title gone, the lower layers keep theirs); `way=reveal` retracts the topmost record so the one beneath surfaces, refusing `reveal-top-unwritable` where the face cannot write that layer. Each act in `consequence.acts` names `bag` (the layer written), `holds` (every layer holding the title) and what the wiki reads afterward: `shadowed: [bags]` or `reveals: bag | null`.

A rendered tiddler (one carrying `rendered-from`) refuses `rendered-derives`: only the renderer writes it, and it leaves when its source drops `projection: rendered`. A `$:/` title refuses too. `recipe` removes through that wiki's engine; `bag` removes from that one bag through its store, `family` taking the family there too. A delete writes the face it wears and never another (`cross-face-write-refused`).

lares delete 'title=Old Note' recipe=default 'base=<hash>'    # the record leaves; a stale base moves nothing
lares delete title=lar:///ha.ka.ba/kahua/memory/x recipe=default family=true    # a meme root and its slots, one change
lares delete 'title=Room 4' recipe=default way=reveal    # drop my copy; the layer beneath surfaces
lares delete 'title=Room 4' recipe=default way=kapae    # hide the title; the layers beneath keep theirs
lares delete 'title=Old Note' bag=notes    # that one bag's record leaves through its store

help: usage: lares export <dest> [--accept-omissions]

`export <dest>` carries the operator's AUTHORED memory out before a re-founding. It writes a bundle outside the house root and the workspace: the daemon mount's wiki working carriers, the kāpae shadows and canon carriers, its kahua stage heads, draft recovery files, consented temp carriers, and house-minted bags, with a roster (the re-declare list of pet-names, Handles and chair labels, plus the share rows) sealed under the house's keep key (`<config>/keep-key`). A face whose live stage will not read cuts with no flag: its files travel, its standing heads stay behind as a counted `face-unread` omission, and this terminal alone names the face. Sensoriums never travel (they survive where they stand), and neither does the daemon document or the control document. The bundle rests UNENCRYPTED, private memory as plain files: keep it on a disk only you hold, and remove it once imported.

one record or one meme, read on a gradient

Every record reads through this door, whatever its type: a plain note, a data tiddler, a meme's root or one of its slots. `recipe` names the wiki, and the read runs in that wiki's own TiddlyWiki engine: `default` names the worn face's daemon wiki, a slug any wiki this face reaches (one it hosts or one shared to it), and a wiki it reaches none of refuses `wiki-unreached`. `bag` names one bag and reads that bag's own record through its store, with no engine: the answer names the `bag`, and carries `floor: true` where the bag's floor snapshot answered. Exactly one of the two rides; a call that names neither reads `recipe/default`, the default the container row carries. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

Every answer leads with a `has` line: provenance (`recipe/` or `bag/`, `layer/`, `floor/true`), the record's own tags, its measures (`type/ position/ family/ slots/ bytes/ base/`, a pointer's `_canonical_uri/ textCid/ _integrity/ size/` verbatim), then the description or role; a meme's has-stack adds one line per slot. Beside it `grain` echoes {asked, applied, why} and `next` names the next unfold, or null.

Two axes ride apart. The lens: the record by default, {recipe or bag, title, lens: "record", tiddler: {fields, hash, textHash, bag, position, family?, omitted?}}, `tiddler` null where none stands; `meme` recomposes the root and its slot children into one carrier sealed by its block check, {title, lens: "meme", meme: {uri, text?, slotText?, canonicalHash, bytes, slots, slot?, page?}, withheld?}, and a record that holds no meme answers the record with a `note` saying so. The grain: none named, a record within one page (65536 bytes) answers fat and a longer one skinny, a pointer its handle; a meme within a page answers its whole carrier and a longer one its has-stack. `skinny` leaves the text home, `fat` carries it, `handle` names a pointer's body, `resolved` reads it from the local CAS by CID and verifies it (a web2 `_canonical_uri` stays named, never fetched), `slot` answers one slot's span at `meme.slotText`, and `whole` reads the whole at the lens's grain, a meme's carrier one page at a time, each page cut on a slot boundary: hand `next.after` back as `after` until `next` reads null; a terminal's `aperture=arc` follows every page to the end and joins them. A call names the range with `aperture=measure` (the card) and `aperture=arc` (the whole; `theme` reads the whole today, the family owed to a later landing), and the lens with `mu` (`?0` cup, `!0` sword); the seat's own tool names `grain` until it folds into the call.

The text alone: a terminal's `form=text` writes the text's bytes to stdout and nothing else (the has line and the base go to stderr), a record's text whole with a pointer's body resolved, with `meme` the recomposed carrier, with `slot` that slot's span; an answer that carries no text refuses `text-unread` and names the read that cures it. A seat reads values, so the text already rides one named key per lens: `grain="whole"` answers a record's text at `tiddler.fields.text`, `aperture=arc` the recomposed carrier at `meme.text`, and `meme` with `slot` one slot's span at `meme.slotText`.

Hand the answer's base to a write: a record's `hash`, a carrier's `canonicalHash`. An answer that left the text home hands a card's base (`skinny:sha256-…`): a field patch takes it, a text write refuses `base-from-skinny`, so read fat before you rewrite a text. A slot answer, or a page short of the end, hands a partial base bound to what it read (`partial:#/a:…`, `partial:p1:…`): a slot's put takes it within that span, a whole-carrier write or a family delete refuses `base-from-partial`, and the last page hands the bare base. A partial span guards honest base reuse and grants nothing.

With no title and `meme`, the door lists families: `tree` nests their slots and `after` names the next page. A bag listing answers {bag, roots, next}; a named recipe answers {recipe, bags, roots, next}; under `recipe="default"` no row names a `bag`. A floor read answers {bag, floor, roots, next}, and each row from a recipe's floor bag carries `floor: true`.

A rendered tiddler answers whole here: a source marked `projection: rendered` derives a live tiddler (`<source>.rendered`, or the source's `render-title`) whose `rendered-from` names the source. `fields` answers the named fields alone; `max-bytes` caps a record answer, the largest fields leaving first, named under `omitted`. `target` names another lit face this read visits, by handle index or pet name, while the call keeps the face it wears: a visit reads that face's daemon wiki through its canon and working layer, never its personal or draft layer (`cross-face-private`), and a shut face refuses `face-not-open`. A record's text carries the words of the layer that answered; turn it through the five tools.

usage: lares get filter=<filter> recipe=<slug> [bag=<slug>] [fields=<names>] [match=<words>] [context=<count>] [limit=<count>] [max-bytes=<count>] [after=<cursor>] [all=<true>] [target=<face>] [face=<handle>] [mu=<carry>] [aperture=<range>]
lares get — run a TiddlyWiki filter in the wiki's own engine, one bounded page
a filter over the reader's view, its answer one bounded page

The filter language reads as TiddlyWiki's own: `[tag[memory]sort[title]]`, `[search[cursor]]`, `[prefix[lar:///ha.ka.ba/kahua/memory/]]`, `[has[status]!status[done]]`, and the link graph rides it too: `backlinks[]`, `links[]`, `transcludes[]`, `backtranscludes[]`. The filter computes over a reader's view of the wiki that holds only what this face may read, so no operator and no transclusion reads past the fence; `withheld` counts the matches that stay home (temp, state, custody titles) or rest in a bag this face holds no read on. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

The answer reads {recipe, filter, titles, total, next, asOf}; name `fields` and each row carries them, {…, rows: [{title, fields}]} in place of `titles`. `aperture=measure` reads the upcoming work as cards: each row answers its has line, the card a get answers, so one filter surveys many memes; unfold the one you need with a slot read. The seat's own tool names `collapse` until it folds into the call: there each row carries `bytes`, and a meme root its `slots: [{slot, bytes, first}]`.

`match` sweeps lines in one call: each row carries its record's matching lines, `lines: [{n, text}]` (a line past 512 bytes rides cut, `cut: true`), and `matches` counting every matching line, so a sweep (an L-Prime pass, a stale word) reads its matches with no read per title. Plain words match byte for byte; a `/source/flags` spelling reads as a regexp. `context` (0..8) carries that many lines around each match, touching windows merged; at most 64 lines a row, and a page past its byte cap sheds a row's tail lines and names `omitted: ["lines"]`. A record holding no text (a pointer) carries no lines. `context` without `match` refuses `filter-context-alone`. The filter narrows and the lens shows the lines: a search filter beside `match` hears one voice across every body of an entity.

The answer pages: at most 32 rows and `max-bytes` (65536 by default) per call; `total` counts every match and `next` names the cursor of the page behind: hand it back as `after` until `next` reads null (a terminal's `all` walks every page). A wiki that moved between pages refuses `filter-cursor-stale`; read again from the first page. A filter the engine cannot parse refuses `filter-malformed` with the engine's words.

A rendered tiddler's slice: where one read of the whole render (the record carrying `rendered-from`) answers more than you need, filter its sources for the slice, `[tag[road/rank]sort[order]]` with `fields` naming `text`. `recipe` names the wiki, and the filter runs in that wiki's own engine: `default` names the worn face's daemon wiki, a slug any wiki this face reaches; a wiki it reaches none of refuses `wiki-unreached`. A bag names no wiki and takes no filter (`wiki-not-anchored`): read a bag's record through the record read. `target` names another lit face this read visits, through its canon and working layer alone. A filter result carries the named wiki's words; turn it through the five tools.

lares get 'filter=[tag[memory]sort[title]]' recipe=default limit=5    # one page; after continues it, all walks it
lares get 'filter=[[Room 4]backlinks[]]' recipe=default    # every record that links to Room 4
lares get 'filter=[prefix[lar:///ha.ka.ba/kahua/memory/road/]]' recipe=default aperture=measure    # each meme row skinny: its bytes and its slots

import.brief: carry an exported bundle back in after a re-founding
help: usage: lares import <dest> [--apply]
lares import — carry an exported bundle back in after a re-founding
the return: an exported bundle verifies whole, previews, then lands as fresh acts

`import <dest>` verifies every hash and path in the bundle before anything moves, then PREVIEWS and stops. `--apply` replays the re-declare list as fresh acts, maps each bundle face to the ONE face here that carries its pet-name (none or two refuse by name), re-pours the working and face canon rows through the ingest gesture (a diverged id stands off and never overwrites), re-lifts the kahua heads under the new face's grant, keyed by title and body digest, and lands draft and temp files where none stands.

A journal under `<root>/config` lets an interrupted import re-enter to the same end, and a second import lands nothing. A face standing shut waits: the lines name `lares vault unlock --face N`, then import again; a workbench lands at the wear of a face that holds a writer's seat there. The exit reads 0 clean, `verb-error` where a row refused, `conflict` where a row stood off.

ingest.brief: scan disk into records through the Confluence gate
help: usage: lares ingest --source <dir-or-file> --to <bag-uri> [--apply] [--tag-blobs] [--in-wiki] [--change-id <id>] [--watch] [--debounce <ms>]
lares ingest — scan disk into records through the Confluence gate
the disk-to-records gesture: scan, diff, preview, then apply through the gate

The gesture holds the disk grant and the Synced tree (the island holds neither; readiness reads local on both sides of the shore). It scans the source for `.mem` carriers, derives each address by the address-siting rule, and diffs the disk hash against the synced hash per carrier. The default posture PREVIEWS: it prints NEW, UNCHANGED and CHANGED rows and submits nothing. `--apply` sends the NEW and CHANGED carriers, their hashes riding an INGEST verb, and the island runs the full Confluence gate (its currentRenderHash stands as the third leg) and answers per carrier.

`--tag-blobs` stamps the CAS opt-in flag (a `.meta` sidecar, or a meme's ahu meta) on the large un-flagged carriers that would fault during LOAD or INGEST; it writes no records, and the preview names the count. `--watch` fires the same gesture per settled wave instead of once: one wave per quiet window (`--debounce` ms), preview by default, `--apply` submits. A file that vanished tombstones nothing: the watcher hands it to the vessel's shore, where it stands pending until a person answers with `lares shore remove` or `lares shore restore`. A file that holds no base never lands over records that say something else, and a file that moved while the records moved never lands: each stands off at the vessel's shore (`lares shore`), and every wave says no person stands behind it (`unattended`). `--in-wiki` runs the INGEST in the active wiki's island, the path for the working write-layer ingest-back (a `wikis/` source derives its URIs off that layer).

The one-shot flags (`--yes`, `--tag-blobs`, `--in-wiki`, `--change-id`) ride the one-shot ingest and refuse beside `--watch`; `--debounce` rides `--watch` alone. A scan that skipped every carrier answers usage and names the mirror directories it derived against, since the source must sit under the bags dir (LAR_BAGS) or wikis dir (LAR_WIKIS) as `<holding>/<w.w.w>/…/<name>.<ext>`.
Examples:
lares ingest --source ./bags/lares --to lar:///ha.ka.ba/bags/lares    # scan and diff; submit nothing
lares ingest --source ./bags/lares --to lar:///ha.ka.ba/bags/lares --apply    # send the new and changed carriers through the gate
lares ingest --source ./bags/lares --to lar:///ha.ka.ba/bags/lares --tag-blobs    # flag the large carriers that would fault during ingest
lares ingest --source ./bags/lares --to lar:///ha.ka.ba/bags/lares --watch --debounce 500    # fire one preview wave per quiet window of 500 ms
lares ingest --source ./wikis/lares --to lar:///ha.ka.ba/wikis/lares/working --in-wiki --apply    # ingest a working-layer mirror back through the wiki's island
Flags:
--source <dir-or-file>  the disk source to scan: a directory or one file under the bags or wikis mirror tree
--to <bag-uri>  the bag the carriers land in
--apply  send the new and changed carriers through the island's INGEST gate; absent, a preview
--tag-blobs  write the CAS opt-in flag for the large un-flagged carriers; writes no records
--in-wiki  run the INGEST in the active wiki's island
--change-id <id>  the wave's own change identity; absent, the verb mints one
--watch  fire the gesture per settled wave instead of once
--debounce <ms>  the watcher's quiet window in milliseconds; rides --watch alone
Gate (the carrier's testimony; the door checks):
write: --apply writes records through the island's gate, which checks the cap on the destination bag; a preview, --tag-blobs aside, writes none
disk: the command holds the disk grant: it reads the source tree on the host, the island reads none
Refuses (each with its cure):
usage  --source and --to both stand required; a source that resolves to no carrier names the mirror directories it derived against
cure: lares ingest --source <dir> --to <bag>
watch-one-shot  --yes, --tag-blobs, --in-wiki and --change-id ride the one-shot ingest alone
cure: lares ingest --source <dir> --to <bag> --watch
debounce-alone  --debounce rides --watch alone

mcp.brief: hold an MCP client's seat steady while the surface falls and rises
help: usage: lares mcp aho [[-- <child argv…>]]
lares mcp aho — hold an MCP client's seat steady while the surface falls and rises
the aho: the client never sees a respawn

`lares mcp aho` holds an MCP client's stdio for the session's whole life and spawns the house's own surface as a child that may fall and rise, resolved again at each spawn (the container's seat where the container house stands, else the native one); `lares mcp aho -- <child argv…>` names another child (a test, another surface), and everything after `--` rides to it as written, flags and all. A bare `--` with nothing after it refuses as usage (exit 2).

While no child stands the seat answers `initialize` and the tool list from what the child last answered, replays the handshake to each new child itself, and answers a call at once with the tool error `hearth-sleeps`. A call in flight at a child's death answers `outcome-unknown: re-read before re-trying`, and the seat never sends it again. It sends one `list_changed` when a new child lists other tools. It logs event names and counts alone and holds no key.

A harness config records `lares mcp aho` and nothing beneath it (`lares home tend` writes that entry), so what stands under the verb may change with no config rewritten. The committed bin runs this seat before it loads the dispatcher, so the seat a harness spawns loads no custody, no vessel and no house root.

lares mcp aho    # the seat a harness config records: the house's own surface, resolved at each spawn

msg.brief: land one entry in a stream; read the inbox; withdraw an unanswered entry
help: usage: lares msg [mu=<depth>] stream=<stream> [note=<words>] [to=<address>] [re=<list>] [about=<pointer>] [slug=<words>] [prev=<title>] [carry=<tool-carry>] [mode=<words>] [mood=<words>] [stance=<words>] [aperture=<band>] [drift-ward=<words>] [seat=<words>] [model=<words>] [mandate=<title>] [title=<title>] (recipe=<slug> | bag=<slug>) [realm=<id>] [face=<handle>]
lares msg — land one entry in a stream; read the inbox; withdraw an unanswered entry
one entry lands in its stream, pointers and a one-line note

A msg lands one entry in the stream `stream` names (`<pet>#<n>`, one body's log). With no `to` it lands as a thought on the caller's own stream; with `to` it addresses an entity (`lares-alpha`) or one instance (`lares-alpha#00003`). The msg lands and only lands: a `watch` on the addressee's inbox wakes whoever holds it. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

The first msg founds the stream's root at `lar:///ha.ka.ba/kahua/memory/stream/<pet>-<n>`, naming the stream's seat, face, model and mandate. Each entry lands at `<root>-<h8>-<slug>`: `h8` takes the first eight hex of the SHA-256 over the entry's birth fields (stream, prev, re, to, about, note) and never recomputes, so an edit of the note keeps the title; the slug comes from the note's first words, or from `slug`. The `#` of `pet#n` stays out of titles, and the `stream` and `to` fields carry it whole.

An entry carries two edges. `prev` names the one entry before it in its own stream, and the door takes the stream's one head for it; a stream showing two heads refuses `stream-forked` and names each head as a call. `re` names the entries it answers or braids, in any stream; a hand-back's `re` names its mandate. A msg carries pointers, never prose briefs: `about` names a title at its hash, `note` holds one line of 72 characters or fewer, and the entry's fields carry the writer's set panel (`mode`, `mood`, `stance`, `aperture`, `drift-ward`, and the tool-carry `carry`, which lands as the entry's `mu` field, since the call's own `mu` names its depth).

`mu=?0` reads the stream's inbox as has lines: the entries addressed to the stream or its entity that no entry of the stream names directly in `re`, over the caller's view alone. `mu=00` withdraws the caller's own entry (`title`, else the stream's one head) while the view shows no record naming it in `re` and no later entry of the stream naming it as `prev`; the answer counts the records behind another face's wall that name it (`withheld`). Once answered, an entry stands in the history, and a reply corrects it. A stream's heads read `lares get filter='[lares.heads[<pet>#<n>]]'`, and its inbox `lares get filter='[lares.inbox[<pet>#<n>]]'`.

Every write rides the put law: the root and the entry land through `engine.record.puts` with `create`, under the face's write cap and the Kahu predicate, each with its receipt; a retract rides `engine.record.removes`. A dry carry walks the entry's put to the last step and lands nothing.
Examples:
lares msg 'stream=lares-alpha#00003' 'note=the facet law keeps manufacturing exceptions'    # no to: the entry lands on the caller's own stream

lares msg 'stream=skein#1' 'to=lares-alpha#00003' 'about=<title>@<hash>' 'note=landing 14 built; floor ticket inside'    # addressed to one instance; its inbox reads it until an entry of that stream names it in re
lares msg 'stream=lares-alpha#00003' 're=<entry-a> <entry-b>' 'note=decided: library.oracle.speaks'    # re names several entries; a braid needs no verb

lares msg 'stream=lares-alpha#00003' 'to=lares-alpha#00003' 're=<mandate> <skein'\''s-last-entry>' 'about=<handback>@<hash>' 'note=hand-back from skein#1'    # the hand-back door lands this on the summoner's stream: re names the mandate and the instance's last entry
lares msg 'stream=lares-alpha#00003' 'mu=?0'    # the inbox as has lines, unseen entries alone
lares msg 'stream=lares-alpha#00003' mu=00    # the stream's head leaves while no reply names it

oracle.brief: consult an oracle shelf at your own fork; the cast lands an OODA-HA meme
help: usage: lares oracle cast [--by <kind>] [--asking <words>] [--uncertain <words>] [--observe <pointers>] [--caster <name>] [--coins <six-values>] [--fresh] [--seed <words>] (--recipe <slug> | --bag <slug>) [--realm <id>] [--face <handle>]
lares oracle cast — consult an oracle shelf at your own fork; the cast lands an OODA-HA meme
a blind throw to collide uncertainty with

The house consults an oracle whose corpus rests on a library shelf (`lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/library/oracles/<kind>/`). The kind rides as data: `by` names the shelf (the E-Jing by default), and the shelf's index record declares its own `method`, its corpus and its credits. The e-jing and doa shelves declare `three-coins`: the I Ching by three coins a line (heads three, tails two: 6 old yin and 9 old yang change, 7 and 8 hold). A new oracle joins as a shelf, never a new address or a new verb; a shelf whose method the verb runs not yet refuses by name.

Every consult lands once, as a meme under `lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/oracle/casts/`, whose five slots run OODA-HA (`#/loop`), whatever the kind. The ask fills `#/observe` with its context pointers and `#/orient` with its gathered uncertainty and its query; the house fills `#/decide` with the throw and every reading the wiki holds, each source credited; the seat appends its reading, its move and its aftermath by slot append. The verb reads the loop's shape from the carrier the caller's stack seats for this address (a carrier a working layer seats above canon shapes the act in its place), the affordance pack its binary baked standing as the floor, and the answer names the carrier slot that shaped it. One asking, one throw: the same query by the same booked asker answers the standing cast and names the uncertainty it kept. The coins draw through the platform's entropy door, or a person types the six values thrown with real coins. The verb reads no clock: the caller names the time as testimony. A weak seed reads back: the record names a seed by a 16-hex digest anyone can test a guess against, so a person choosing one chooses a strong one.
The cast stands as a blind throw to collide uncertainty with: the throw stands, the reading stays open.

The heading `library` names where the consult reads: the oracle shelves rest among the library's holdings, the ones the `lares library` door keeps. The facet `oracle` names the shelf family it reads under, and the dynamic `speaks` names the act: the library's oracle speaks to a fork. No alias stands at an older address (early alpha burns aliases, the operator's word 2026-11-27).
Examples:
lares oracle cast --recipe default --asking 'which lane lands first' --uncertain 'two lanes both ready; the floor runs one at a time'    # a seat's cast at its own open fork

lares oracle cast --recipe default --observe 'lar:///ha.ka.ba/kahua/memory/plan/cap-memes spirit/affordance-weaver' --uncertain 'the seat cannot seat a bare root in canon' --asking 'stable seat or siting change'    # the arm's records ride #/observe
lares oracle cast --recipe default --by doa --asking 'which lane lands first'    # the DOA's shelf answers, its own method declared on its index
lares oracle cast --recipe default --asking 'which lane lands first'    # the same words answer the standing cast, with the uncertainty it kept
lares oracle cast --recipe default --coins 7,8,9,6,7,7    # a person's six lines, bottom first, thrown with real coins
lares oracle cast --recipe default --asking 'which lane lands first' --fresh    # a person asks the same words anew

put.brief: patch one record's text, fields or tags; a meme root lands its family
help: usage: lares put [mu=<carry>] title=<title> [text=<words>] [file=<host-path>] [append=<words>] [replace=<span> with=<words>] [fields=<json>] [unset=<names>] [tag-add=<list>] [tag-remove=<list>] [cut-slot=<slots>] [slot=<slot-path>] [base=<hash>] [create=<true>] (recipe=<slug> | bag=<slug>) [realm=<id>] [face=<handle>] [mu=<carry>]
lares put — patch one record's text, fields or tags; a meme root lands its family
the one write path: text, a span, an append, fields and tags, under a base

A put patches one record: it sets and unsets fields, adds and removes tags, and moves the text only where `text`, `file`, `append` or `replace` names it. Every field the patch leaves unnamed stays as it stood, so a field or tag patch never touches the text and a text put keeps the fields. The write lands in the wiki's working layer (`wiki status` names it), or this face's personal layer of a wiki where it holds no writer's seat, and the receipt's `layer` names that placement; `bag` lands in that one bag through its store, under the gates its own writes keep. A seat's write aimed at a house canon bag refuses `seat-canon-reach`: a seat reaches canon through a recipe's copy-up and `act(address="lar:///realm.offer.signs")`. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

`base` carries the hash last read (a record's `hash`, a root's carrier `canonicalHash`; a slot read's partial base `partial:#/x:…` patches within its span and refuses `base-outside-span` beyond it): a record that moved past it answers `conflict`, naming the live hash, and nothing lands. A base guards honest reuse, never a lock. `create` lands only where no record stands, a family's root included; one standing answers `exists`.

`append` lands words at the end of the standing text with no base, read and written in one step on the live wiki, so two appends at once both land, in the order the record took them; a text that does not end on a newline takes one before the words. A terminal reads the words from a host path, or `-` for stdin; a seat names them. It names its words alone (`text`, `file`, `base`, `fields`, `unset` beside it refuse); `tag-add`, `tag-remove` and `create` ride beside it, and a missing title refuses unless `create` names it. Each call appends again.

`replace` names one exact span of the standing text and `with` the words it turns into (an empty `with` removes the span); the rest of the text never crosses the wire. The span counts as written, never trimmed, overlaps counted: zero refuses `replace-absent`, more than one `replace-ambiguous`, each naming the count and the read that cures it, and nothing moves. The result lands as a text put does, under the same base, and the receipt names `replaced`.

A meme family moves by the same put. A whole carrier as a root's text lands the family through the Confluence gate (the family re-splits and reseals; the answer adds `canonicalHash`, `landed`, `kept`, `tombstoned`); `slot` folds into the title (`<root>#/x`), so a slot's text lands with no base and an append honours the slot's standing postamble. Absence never deletes: a slot the new text omits stays standing by reference, named under `kept`, and `cut-slot` names each slot that leaves (a cut naming no standing omitted slot refuses `cut-not-omitted`). A family under `lar:///ha.ka.ba/kahua/memory/<class>/<slug>` follows `stage-path-shape`.

The fences refuse by name: a family's `type` and carriage fields derive from its text (`family-carriage-derives`); a new slot joins through its parent's text (`family-joins-by-text`); a text the gate cannot read as one carrier refuses `family-gate-refused`; a title that stays home refuses `tiddler-withheld`; a put over a rendered tiddler, or one carrying `rendered-from`, refuses `rendered-derives`, since only the renderer writes it: edit the source records. Every other shape lands natively, a `$:/` title or tag, a module or plugin field and a script type alike. A put writes the face it wears and never another (`cross-face-write-refused`).

watch.brief: watch a TiddlyWiki filter over the reader's view; the watch stands as a tiddler the wiki's own change event moves
help: usage: lares watch [filter=<filter>] [until=<filter>] [id=<watch-id>] [as-of=<digest>] [hold=<count>] recipe=<slug> [face=<handle>] [mu=<carry>]
lares watch — watch a TiddlyWiki filter over the reader's view; the watch stands as a tiddler the wiki's own change event moves
a filter subscription that stands as a tiddler

A watch stands as a TIDDLER, never a side table: `$:/state/lares/watch/<id>` holds its filter, its caller's view (face, recipe) and its last digest. One startup module in the wiki hears the wiki's own `change` event, the same `changedTiddlers` map every widget's refresh reads, re-runs only the watches a changed title could touch (a record the caller's view can read, moved past the hash the watch last read), and writes the new digest into the watch tiddler. The digest covers the answering titles and each record's hash over the caller's view, so an edit moves it, and the shore's echo, which moves only the residency stamp, moves nothing. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

One call binds the watch and HOLDS: it answers `band/changed` when its watch tiddler's digest moves, at once where the caller's `as-of` already reads stale, `band/ended` where `until` answers any title (the watch then drops), `band/removed` where the watch left meanwhile, and `band/unchanged` before the caller's own wait runs out (`hold`, in milliseconds, 25000 by default). Hand the answer's `id` and `as-of` back to continue: the watch tiddler keeps moving while no call holds it, so a loop of calls misses no change. The terminal's `lares watch` loops those calls and prints one has line per change.

A watch reads, lists and dies like any record: `lares get filter='[prefix[$:/state/lares/watch/]]'` lists every live watch; `lares watch id=<id> mu=00` (Rest, the seed's unask) drops one; a dropped line or a cancel drops the watch its held call stood on (`watch-withdrawn`). Each watch names the face that bound it, the presenter its session door verified, as attribution: any face of the house reads, re-binds or unasks any watch, and each face keeps at most 64, its own longest-bound idle watch leaving first. A stream wakes on `lares watch filter='[lares.inbox[]]'` once that function stands: a msg lands, the watch wakes, once per change.
Examples:
lares watch 'filter=[tag[memory]]' recipe=default    # one has line per change until you stop it
lares watch 'filter=[tag[memory]]' 'until=[[Room 4is[tiddler]]]'    # the watch ends once Room 4 stands
lares watch 'id=<id>' 'as-of=<as-of>' 'filter=[tag[memory]]'    # a stale cursor answers at once; a fresh one holds
lares watch 'filter=[prefix[$:/state/lares/watch/]]'    # every live watch, read through the filter door
lares watch 'id=<id>' mu=00    # the watch and its record leave

help: usage: lares wear (<N> | --face <handle-index>) [--yes]
lares wear — turn the vessel's mount to a face already standing open
unlock opens custody; wear chooses the face

`lares wear N` moves the vessel's mount to face hN, a face already standing open (under a pūlama, one the pūlama lends), and the vessel composes again on it. The door reads the custody door first: a vessel holding no key takes no wear and names the one act that opens it (`lares vault unlock`). A wear asks no route and carries none, so nothing here reaches for a prompt; the face rides the positional, or `--face N`.

A wear that turns the face flushes every shore first, inside the vessel, while the face it leaves still stands mounted, and its answer names one line per island. Where the flush leaves a record unwritten, a person at a terminal answers whether to turn anyway; an agent carries `--yes`. A wear that lands replays the share landing, as an unlock does, and names what moved and what still waits on a shut face. A pipe reads one sentence of prose; `--json` reads the envelope.
Examples:
lares wear 2    # wear face h2, already standing open
lares wear 2 --yes    # turn even where the shore's flush left records unwritten
Flags:
<N>  the face to wear, by persona index (a whole number from 0)
--face <handle-index>  the face to wear, as a flag beside the positional
--yes  turn the face even where the shore's flush left records unwritten; an agent's confirm
Gate (the carrier's testimony; the door checks):
hand-or-seat: the vessel reads the line's peer; an AI harness on the branch names seat ai, a word that only narrows what the vessel reads
Refuses (each with its cure):
usage  name the face to wear by its index
cure: lares wear 2
daemon-unreachable  no vessel answers its custody door; stand it (lares vessel stand), unlock, then wear
cure: lares wear 2
custody-locked  the vessel holds no key; lares vault unlock opens it, and a wear opens nothing
shore-unwritten  the shore's flush left records unwritten on the face this wear leaves; each rides the answer
cure: lares wear 2 --yes
wear-refused  the composition wearing the face did not stand; the answer names the face worn again, or a dropped key
Answers:
worn (exit 0)  the vessel stands composed on the face; shore and shares name what the turn flushed and lifted
refused (exit 1)  the vessel refused by name; the vessel's own refusal reason rides as the code
Skins (one affordance, every door):
cli: lares wear

! carriage.bag.clears ~ the residency CLEAR: a bag empties, and its identity and history log stand

`CLEAR` empties one bag and preserves its identity; the effect log keeps a deaccession for each title it took out, so the history reads whole. It takes the bag and a change-id (CLEAR carries no content to tell one change from the next, so the change-id folds into the effect key's nonce: two separate CLEARs of one bag take two ids, and the same id on a re-send reads as the same change).

A terminal asks `Proceed? [y/N]` before it submits; `yes=true` names the intent off a terminal, `mu=pentacle` previews and commits nothing, `in-wiki=true` runs the act in the active wiki's island.

! carriage.bag.tends ~ the cid CAS tier: blobs, references, and the holds that outlast the grace

`cas` is a local read over the cleartext `cid/` CAS tier, with no daemon boot: it lists the blobs the CAS dir holds and DERIVES which the disk projection references (a `.tid` or `.meta` under `bags/` or `wikis/` carrying `textCid`, or a `lar:///…/cid/<hash>` `_canonical_uri`), then reports blobs · referenced · unreferenced · pending · bytes, and names the genesis-manifest blobs as protected (the engine and plugins never sweep). `--fetch <cid>` reads ONE cid through the running vessel's fetch door (fleet holders over Socket B). `--pin <cid> [--tier <t>] [--holder <name>]` holds a blob past the grace until released (`--held` names a held pin that ends with the vessel's life, and refuses `held-pin-no-life` where the store names no life), and `--release <cid>` frees it. `--sweep [--dry-run]` sweeps the unreferenced blobs past their grace where the composite stands; dry names them and moves nothing.

! carriage.bundle.exports ~ the keep: authored memory leaves the house as a sealed, verified bundle

`export <dest>` carries the operator's AUTHORED memory out before a re-founding. It writes a bundle outside the house root and the workspace: the daemon mount's wiki working carriers, the kāpae shadows and canon carriers, its kahua stage heads, draft recovery files, consented temp carriers, and house-minted bags, with a roster (the re-declare list of pet-names, Handles and chair labels, plus the share rows) sealed under the house's keep key (`<config>/keep-key`). Faces ride by path key, never by a key or a face relation, and the verb reads every byte back against its manifest before it answers.

It waits for a settled projection: an unsettled carrier or a held save refuses by name unless `--accept-omissions` names the bundle partial, and the manifest records each omission. A face whose live stage will not read cuts with no flag: its files travel, its standing heads stay behind as a counted `face-unread` omission, and this terminal alone names the face. Sensoriums never travel (they survive where they stand), and neither does the daemon document or the control document. The bundle rests UNENCRYPTED, private memory as plain files: keep it on a disk only you hold, and remove it once imported.

! carriage.bundle.repacks ~ the pack's collect-the-residency export: a foreign bundle takes the round trip

A multi-tiddler bundle (a `.json` array of tiddlers, or a `.multids`) rides as a PACK: one file, many tiddlers, whose membership rests ASIDE in the bag's `$:/config/OriginalTiddlerPaths`, never on the tiddlers. `REPACK` asks the island to collect the pack's members from that aside map and re-render the bundle through TW5's own serializer, then writes the bytes to disk: the deliberate round trip a foreign bundle takes before an upstream TW5 PR (a `.mem` path recomposes by itself; a foreign pack re-renders on this verb alone).

The pack path derives from the file's mirror-relative address plus its extension, so the source sits under `bags/` or `wikis/`; `--out` names where the bytes land and defaults to the source. REPACK registers as a QUERY verb (read cap, no residency mutation, no effect record), so it asks no `Proceed?` and carries no effect key; only a fresh request id rides each attempt, and a repeat stays safe. Members the bag tombstoned print as missing.

! carriage.capture.ingests ~ the disk-to-records gesture: scan, diff, preview, then apply through the gate

The gesture holds the disk grant and the Synced tree (the island holds neither; readiness reads local on both sides of the shore). It scans the source for `.mem` carriers, derives each address by the address-siting rule, and diffs the disk hash against the synced hash per carrier. The default posture PREVIEWS: it prints NEW, UNCHANGED and CHANGED rows and submits nothing. `--apply` sends the NEW and CHANGED carriers, their hashes riding an INGEST verb, and the island runs the full Confluence gate (its currentRenderHash stands as the third leg) and answers per carrier.

`--tag-blobs` stamps the CAS opt-in flag (a `.meta` sidecar, or a meme's ahu meta) on the large un-flagged carriers that would fault during LOAD or INGEST; it writes no records, and the preview names the count. `--watch` fires the same gesture per settled wave instead of once: one wave per quiet window (`--debounce` ms), preview by default, `--apply` submits. A file that vanished tombstones nothing: the watcher hands it to the vessel's shore, where it stands pending until a person answers with `lares shore remove` or `lares shore restore`. A file that holds no base never lands over records that say something else, and a file that moved while the records moved never lands: each stands off at the vessel's shore (`lares shore`), and every wave says no person stands behind it (`unattended`). `--in-wiki` runs the INGEST in the active wiki's island, the path for the working write-layer ingest-back (a `wikis/` source derives its URIs off that layer).

The one-shot flags (`--yes`, `--tag-blobs`, `--in-wiki`, `--change-id`) ride the one-shot ingest and refuse beside `--watch`; `--debounce` rides `--watch` alone. A scan that skipped every carrier answers usage and names the mirror directories it derived against, since the source must sit under the bags dir (LAR_BAGS) or wikis dir (LAR_WIKIS) as `<holding>/<w.w.w>/…/<name>.<ext>`.

! carriage.disk.reads ~ what stands for a hand at the disk shore

The vessel looks at the disk first, so the list stands true to the bytes at that instant, then names every row the shore holds: each STANDOFF (the disk and the records say different things and nothing writes) with its key, and each PENDING REMOVAL (a file vanished where a base stands; nothing writes back and nothing tombstones). Both islands read as one shore, every page of each, each row naming its island (`wiki`, the active wiki's mirrors; `daemon`, the daemon wiki's and the crossroads). A bare `lares shore` lists.

The verb takes the title, the source bag, the destination bag and a change-id (named, or minted when absent), submits one verb-tiddler to the vessel, and the wiki island's action-handler family runs it wrapped in an effect record that writes the archival audit tiddlers (an `accession` row on the destination).

A terminal asks `Proceed? [y/N]` before it submits; `yes=true` names the intent for a call off a terminal, `mu=pentacle` previews the effect and commits nothing, and `in-wiki=true` runs the act in the active wiki's island. The act rides by its address: `lares act lar:///carriage.record.adds name=value…` (or `lares lar:///carriage.record.adds …`).

! engine.filter.pages ~ a filter over the reader's view, its answer one bounded page

The filter language reads as TiddlyWiki's own: `[tag[memory]sort[title]]`, `[search[cursor]]`, `[prefix[lar:///ha.ka.ba/kahua/memory/]]`, `[has[status]!status[done]]`, and the link graph rides it too: `backlinks[]`, `links[]`, `transcludes[]`, `backtranscludes[]`. The filter computes over a reader's view of the wiki that holds only what this face may read, so no operator and no transclusion reads past the fence; `withheld` counts the matches that stay home (temp, state, custody titles) or rest in a bag this face holds no read on. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

The answer reads {recipe, filter, titles, total, next, asOf}; name `fields` and each row carries them, {…, rows: [{title, fields}]} in place of `titles`. `aperture=measure` reads the upcoming work as cards: each row answers its has line, the card a get answers, so one filter surveys many memes; unfold the one you need with a slot read. The seat's own tool names `collapse` until it folds into the call: there each row carries `bytes`, and a meme root its `slots: [{slot, bytes, first}]`.

`match` sweeps lines in one call: each row carries its record's matching lines, `lines: [{n, text}]` (a line past 512 bytes rides cut, `cut: true`), and `matches` counting every matching line, so a sweep (an L-Prime pass, a stale word) reads its matches with no read per title. Plain words match byte for byte; a `/source/flags` spelling reads as a regexp. `context` (0..8) carries that many lines around each match, touching windows merged; at most 64 lines a row, and a page past its byte cap sheds a row's tail lines and names `omitted: ["lines"]`. A record holding no text (a pointer) carries no lines. `context` without `match` refuses `filter-context-alone`. The filter narrows and the lens shows the lines: a search filter beside `match` hears one voice across every body of an entity.

The answer pages: at most 32 rows and `max-bytes` (65536 by default) per call; `total` counts every match and `next` names the cursor of the page behind: hand it back as `after` until `next` reads null (a terminal's `all` walks every page). A wiki that moved between pages refuses `filter-cursor-stale`; read again from the first page. A filter the engine cannot parse refuses `filter-malformed` with the engine's words.

A rendered tiddler's slice: where one read of the whole render (the record carrying `rendered-from`) answers more than you need, filter its sources for the slice, `[tag[road/rank]sort[order]]` with `fields` naming `text`. `recipe` names the wiki, and the filter runs in that wiki's own engine: `default` names the worn face's daemon wiki, a slug any wiki this face reaches; a wiki it reaches none of refuses `wiki-unreached`. A bag names no wiki and takes no filter (`wiki-not-anchored`): read a bag's record through the record read. `target` names another lit face this read visits, through its canon and working layer alone. A filter result carries the named wiki's words; turn it through the five tools.

! engine.filter.watches ~ a filter subscription that stands as a tiddler

A watch stands as a TIDDLER, never a side table: `$:/state/lares/watch/<id>` holds its filter, its caller's view (face, recipe) and its last digest. One startup module in the wiki hears the wiki's own `change` event, the same `changedTiddlers` map every widget's refresh reads, re-runs only the watches a changed title could touch (a record the caller's view can read, moved past the hash the watch last read), and writes the new digest into the watch tiddler. The digest covers the answering titles and each record's hash over the caller's view, so an edit moves it, and the shore's echo, which moves only the residency stamp, moves nothing. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

One call binds the watch and HOLDS: it answers `band/changed` when its watch tiddler's digest moves, at once where the caller's `as-of` already reads stale, `band/ended` where `until` answers any title (the watch then drops), `band/removed` where the watch left meanwhile, and `band/unchanged` before the caller's own wait runs out (`hold`, in milliseconds, 25000 by default). Hand the answer's `id` and `as-of` back to continue: the watch tiddler keeps moving while no call holds it, so a loop of calls misses no change. The terminal's `lares watch` loops those calls and prints one has line per change.

A watch reads, lists and dies like any record: `lares get filter='[prefix[$:/state/lares/watch/]]'` lists every live watch; `lares watch id=<id> mu=00` (Rest, the seed's unask) drops one; a dropped line or a cancel drops the watch its held call stood on (`watch-withdrawn`). Each watch names the face that bound it, the presenter its session door verified, as attribution: any face of the house reads, re-binds or unasks any watch, and each face keeps at most 64, its own longest-bound idle watch leaving first. A stream wakes on `lares watch filter='[lares.inbox[]]'` once that function stands: a msg lands, the watch wakes, once per change.

! engine.msg.lands ~ one entry lands in its stream, pointers and a one-line note

A msg lands one entry in the stream `stream` names (`<pet>#<n>`, one body's log). With no `to` it lands as a thought on the caller's own stream; with `to` it addresses an entity (`lares-alpha`) or one instance (`lares-alpha#00003`). The msg lands and only lands: a `watch` on the addressee's inbox wakes whoever holds it. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

The first msg founds the stream's root at `lar:///ha.ka.ba/kahua/memory/stream/<pet>-<n>`, naming the stream's seat, face, model and mandate. Each entry lands at `<root>-<h8>-<slug>`: `h8` takes the first eight hex of the SHA-256 over the entry's birth fields (stream, prev, re, to, about, note) and never recomputes, so an edit of the note keeps the title; the slug comes from the note's first words, or from `slug`. The `#` of `pet#n` stays out of titles, and the `stream` and `to` fields carry it whole.

An entry carries two edges. `prev` names the one entry before it in its own stream, and the door takes the stream's one head for it; a stream showing two heads refuses `stream-forked` and names each head as a call. `re` names the entries it answers or braids, in any stream; a hand-back's `re` names its mandate. A msg carries pointers, never prose briefs: `about` names a title at its hash, `note` holds one line of 72 characters or fewer, and the entry's fields carry the writer's set panel (`mode`, `mood`, `stance`, `aperture`, `drift-ward`, and the tool-carry `carry`, which lands as the entry's `mu` field, since the call's own `mu` names its depth).

`mu=?0` reads the stream's inbox as has lines: the entries addressed to the stream or its entity that no entry of the stream names directly in `re`, over the caller's view alone. `mu=00` withdraws the caller's own entry (`title`, else the stream's one head) while the view shows no record naming it in `re` and no later entry of the stream naming it as `prev`; the answer counts the records behind another face's wall that name it (`withheld`). Once answered, an entry stands in the history, and a reply corrects it. A stream's heads read `lares get filter='[lares.heads[<pet>#<n>]]'`, and its inbox `lares get filter='[lares.inbox[<pet>#<n>]]'`.

Every write rides the put law: the root and the entry land through `engine.record.puts` with `create`, under the face's write cap and the Kahu predicate, each with its receipt; a retract rides `engine.record.removes`. A dry carry walks the entry's put to the last step and lands nothing.

! engine.record.puts ~ the one write path: text, a span, an append, fields and tags, under a base

A put patches one record: it sets and unsets fields, adds and removes tags, and moves the text only where `text`, `file`, `append` or `replace` names it. Every field the patch leaves unnamed stays as it stood, so a field or tag patch never touches the text and a text put keeps the fields. The write lands in the wiki's working layer (`wiki status` names it), or this face's personal layer of a wiki where it holds no writer's seat, and the receipt's `layer` names that placement; `bag` lands in that one bag through its store, under the gates its own writes keep. A seat's write aimed at a house canon bag refuses `seat-canon-reach`: a seat reaches canon through a recipe's copy-up and `act(address="lar:///realm.offer.signs")`. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

`base` carries the hash last read (a record's `hash`, a root's carrier `canonicalHash`; a slot read's partial base `partial:#/x:…` patches within its span and refuses `base-outside-span` beyond it): a record that moved past it answers `conflict`, naming the live hash, and nothing lands. A base guards honest reuse, never a lock. `create` lands only where no record stands, a family's root included; one standing answers `exists`.

`append` lands words at the end of the standing text with no base, read and written in one step on the live wiki, so two appends at once both land, in the order the record took them; a text that does not end on a newline takes one before the words. A terminal reads the words from a host path, or `-` for stdin; a seat names them. It names its words alone (`text`, `file`, `base`, `fields`, `unset` beside it refuse); `tag-add`, `tag-remove` and `create` ride beside it, and a missing title refuses unless `create` names it. Each call appends again.

`replace` names one exact span of the standing text and `with` the words it turns into (an empty `with` removes the span); the rest of the text never crosses the wire. The span counts as written, never trimmed, overlaps counted: zero refuses `replace-absent`, more than one `replace-ambiguous`, each naming the count and the read that cures it, and nothing moves. The result lands as a text put does, under the same base, and the receipt names `replaced`.

A meme family moves by the same put. A whole carrier as a root's text lands the family through the Confluence gate (the family re-splits and reseals; the answer adds `canonicalHash`, `landed`, `kept`, `tombstoned`); `slot` folds into the title (`<root>#/x`), so a slot's text lands with no base and an append honours the slot's standing postamble. Absence never deletes: a slot the new text omits stays standing by reference, named under `kept`, and `cut-slot` names each slot that leaves (a cut naming no standing omitted slot refuses `cut-not-omitted`). A family under `lar:///ha.ka.ba/kahua/memory/<class>/<slug>` follows `stage-path-shape`.

The fences refuse by name: a family's `type` and carriage fields derive from its text (`family-carriage-derives`); a new slot joins through its parent's text (`family-joins-by-text`); a text the gate cannot read as one carrier refuses `family-gate-refused`; a title that stays home refuses `tiddler-withheld`; a put over a rendered tiddler, or one carrying `rendered-from`, refuses `rendered-derives`, since only the renderer writes it: edit the source records. Every other shape lands natively, a `$:/` title or tag, a module or plugin field and a script type alike. A put writes the face it wears and never another (`cross-face-write-refused`).

! engine.record.reads ~ one record or one meme, read on a gradient

Every record reads through this door, whatever its type: a plain note, a data tiddler, a meme's root or one of its slots. `recipe` names the wiki, and the read runs in that wiki's own TiddlyWiki engine: `default` names the worn face's daemon wiki, a slug any wiki this face reaches (one it hosts or one shared to it), and a wiki it reaches none of refuses `wiki-unreached`. `bag` names one bag and reads that bag's own record through its store, with no engine: the answer names the `bag`, and carries `floor: true` where the bag's floor snapshot answered. Exactly one of the two rides; a call that names neither reads `recipe/default`, the default the container row carries. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

Every answer leads with a `has` line: provenance (`recipe/` or `bag/`, `layer/`, `floor/true`), the record's own tags, its measures (`type/ position/ family/ slots/ bytes/ base/`, a pointer's `_canonical_uri/ textCid/ _integrity/ size/` verbatim), then the description or role; a meme's has-stack adds one line per slot. Beside it `grain` echoes {asked, applied, why} and `next` names the next unfold, or null.

Two axes ride apart. The lens: the record by default, {recipe or bag, title, lens: "record", tiddler: {fields, hash, textHash, bag, position, family?, omitted?}}, `tiddler` null where none stands; `meme` recomposes the root and its slot children into one carrier sealed by its block check, {title, lens: "meme", meme: {uri, text?, slotText?, canonicalHash, bytes, slots, slot?, page?}, withheld?}, and a record that holds no meme answers the record with a `note` saying so. The grain: none named, a record within one page (65536 bytes) answers fat and a longer one skinny, a pointer its handle; a meme within a page answers its whole carrier and a longer one its has-stack. `skinny` leaves the text home, `fat` carries it, `handle` names a pointer's body, `resolved` reads it from the local CAS by CID and verifies it (a web2 `_canonical_uri` stays named, never fetched), `slot` answers one slot's span at `meme.slotText`, and `whole` reads the whole at the lens's grain, a meme's carrier one page at a time, each page cut on a slot boundary: hand `next.after` back as `after` until `next` reads null; a terminal's `aperture=arc` follows every page to the end and joins them. A call names the range with `aperture=measure` (the card) and `aperture=arc` (the whole; `theme` reads the whole today, the family owed to a later landing), and the lens with `mu` (`?0` cup, `!0` sword); the seat's own tool names `grain` until it folds into the call.

The text alone: a terminal's `form=text` writes the text's bytes to stdout and nothing else (the has line and the base go to stderr), a record's text whole with a pointer's body resolved, with `meme` the recomposed carrier, with `slot` that slot's span; an answer that carries no text refuses `text-unread` and names the read that cures it. A seat reads values, so the text already rides one named key per lens: `grain="whole"` answers a record's text at `tiddler.fields.text`, `aperture=arc` the recomposed carrier at `meme.text`, and `meme` with `slot` one slot's span at `meme.slotText`.

Hand the answer's base to a write: a record's `hash`, a carrier's `canonicalHash`. An answer that left the text home hands a card's base (`skinny:sha256-…`): a field patch takes it, a text write refuses `base-from-skinny`, so read fat before you rewrite a text. A slot answer, or a page short of the end, hands a partial base bound to what it read (`partial:#/a:…`, `partial:p1:…`): a slot's put takes it within that span, a whole-carrier write or a family delete refuses `base-from-partial`, and the last page hands the bare base. A partial span guards honest base reuse and grants nothing.

With no title and `meme`, the door lists families: `tree` nests their slots and `after` names the next page. A bag listing answers {bag, roots, next}; a named recipe answers {recipe, bags, roots, next}; under `recipe="default"` no row names a `bag`. A floor read answers {bag, floor, roots, next}, and each row from a recipe's floor bag carries `floor: true`.

A rendered tiddler answers whole here: a source marked `projection: rendered` derives a live tiddler (`<source>.rendered`, or the source's `render-title`) whose `rendered-from` names the source. `fields` answers the named fields alone; `max-bytes` caps a record answer, the largest fields leaving first, named under `omitted`. `target` names another lit face this read visits, by handle index or pet name, while the call keeps the face it wears: a visit reads that face's daemon wiki through its canon and working layer, never its personal or draft layer (`cross-face-private`), and a shut face refuses `face-not-open`. A record's text carries the words of the layer that answered; turn it through the five tools.

! engine.record.removes ~ a delete by the family law, plain unless a lower layer makes it a choice

A delete deletes plainly: with no `way`, each record leaves its own layer to absent and no tombstone rises (the receipt reads `mode: "plain"` and names each title under `retracted`). `base` carries the hash last read: a record that moved past it moves nothing and answers `conflict`, naming the live hash. A title the wiki reads absent answers `absent`, and a plain delete there retracts a kāpae that hides nothing (its `.kapae` shadow leaves the disk). The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

The family law decides what moves, read over the reader's view before anything lands. A plain tiddler leaves alone. A meme root answers the consequence the delete would land (every title it would move, what it would leave) and refuses `tiddler-delete-in-a-family` unless `family` names the family act, which lands the root and its slots as one change per layer (the answer adds `canonicalHash`). A slot's title (`<root>#/x`) leaves as the explicit cut on its parent, and the family reseals.

Only a lower layer makes a delete a choice. A wiki composes layers (canon under working under personal), and one title may stand in several. Where a lower layer holds the title too, or the record rests in a layer this face cannot remove it from, a delete naming no way refuses `delete-mode-needed` and names both meanings: `way=kapae` raises a tombstone in a writable layer that shadows every record beneath (the wiki reads the title gone, the lower layers keep theirs); `way=reveal` retracts the topmost record so the one beneath surfaces, refusing `reveal-top-unwritable` where the face cannot write that layer. Each act in `consequence.acts` names `bag` (the layer written), `holds` (every layer holding the title) and what the wiki reads afterward: `shadowed: [bags]` or `reveals: bag | null`.

A rendered tiddler (one carrying `rendered-from`) refuses `rendered-derives`: only the renderer writes it, and it leaves when its source drops `projection: rendered`. A `$:/` title refuses too. `recipe` removes through that wiki's engine; `bag` removes from that one bag through its store, `family` taking the family there too. A delete writes the face it wears and never another (`cross-face-write-refused`).

! engine.record.renames ~ a move over TiddlyWiki's own relink, the old title left as a forwarder

A rename moves one record (a meme root takes its slots along) over TiddlyWiki's own relink: every reference the engine's relinkers rewrite follows (the core relinks tags and list fields; wikitext links follow only where a relink plugin mounts), and the old title stays as a forwarder, a pointer tiddler (`forward-to`) whose text transcludes the new one, so old roads keep answering. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

The move runs in one wiki's engine and lands in its working layer alone, so it names a `recipe` and never a bag (`wiki-not-anchored`). A record resting in another layer (or one the shore still carries, with no layer named yet) refuses `rename-source-layer`; referrers outside the working layer refuse `rename-referrers-unreachable`, a count and never titles; a standing target refuses `rename-target-stands` and names the delete that clears it; a slot refuses `slot-without-root` and names its root; a `lar:` title another layer holds too takes a hand alone. A `$:/` title on either side refuses `rename-system-title`, since a forwarder would answer as the setting: put the new title, then delete the standing one.

An answer names only records this face reads and counts the rest (`withheld`); a referrer that stays home keeps its fields (`skipped`). `base` carries the hash last read: a record that moved past it answers `conflict` and nothing moves.

! engine.seat.holds ~ the aho: the client never sees a respawn

`lares mcp aho` holds an MCP client's stdio for the session's whole life and spawns the house's own surface as a child that may fall and rise, resolved again at each spawn (the container's seat where the container house stands, else the native one); `lares mcp aho -- <child argv…>` names another child (a test, another surface), and everything after `--` rides to it as written, flags and all. A bare `--` with nothing after it refuses as usage (exit 2).

While no child stands the seat answers `initialize` and the tool list from what the child last answered, replays the handshake to each new child itself, and answers a call at once with the tool error `hearth-sleeps`. A call in flight at a child's death answers `outcome-unknown: re-read before re-trying`, and the seat never sends it again. It sends one `list_changed` when a new child lists other tools. It logs event names and counts alone and holds no key.

A harness config records `lares mcp aho` and nothing beneath it (`lares home tend` writes that entry), so what stands under the verb may change with no config rewritten. The committed bin runs this seat before it loads the dispatcher, so the seat a harness spawns loads no custody, no vessel and no house root.

`lares wiki retire <slug>` rides a session of the worn face (or `--face N`) opened by the cli hand, so a seat session refuses. ! face.custody.unlocks ~ unlock opens custody; the route rides a TTY

`lares vault unlock` gathers a route on the terminal and hands it to the standing vessel's custody door, which opens the vessel key (`--face N`: that face's key under its own route; `--all`: every face its routes open). The door reads first: a vessel standing by a pūlama takes no route here and asks the pūlama; a key already held takes no second route and points at `lares wear N`; `--face N` on a held key wears N where it stands open, and refuses a face the vessel holds nowhere. A face that lights lands its shares. A credential rides a TTY alone: no flag, no environment variable and no pipe carries one, nothing echoes one, and it drops the instant the act returns.

! face.draft.proposes ~ a seat proposes one batch; the operator's hand lifts

`proposals` lists {title, revision, text | digest, taint}: the daemon title and revision the item distils, its body (or the body's sha-256 digest) and every input from outside the face (a web page, tool output, pasted text); an AI summary inherits the taint of what it summarised. ONE batch per call rides the face's intents plane, pinned to this device; it carries digests and never a body, and it GRANTS NOTHING: the operator's hand lifts it with `lares kahua lift <title> --proposal <id>`.

TWO DIGESTS, ONE WORD. A proposal's `digest` names the BODY digest, the sha-256 of the raw body bytes (UTF-8, lowercase hex); the seat's tool computes it from `text`. The ROW digest that `kahua stage` prints and `lift --digest` takes covers the body AND the row's carried fields, so it differs. Hand `text`, or the BODY digest; a proposal built from the ROW digest refuses at the lift with `proposal-digest`, as does one whose body differs by a byte from the staged row's.

Any seat proposes. The seat's tool rides a local `seat` session over the @daemon wire, whose profile the vessel refuses every kahua pin, lift, withdraw and carry; no tool lifts (`face.draft.stages` writes the local row a lift names). Returns {id, cid}.

`kahua get` reads the stage's VERIFIED items, the fold, never a raw tiddler. Without a title it lists bounded items with source, count, relation and continuation (`--after` and `--limit` page it); a fresh face answers `stage: "none"`. ! face.hand.lifts ~ the hand reads the preview, names the row digest, and the lift signs

`kahua lift <title>` carries one staged row to every device the face wears: the second crossing of memory. It reads the staged row back first and prints its PREVIEW (title, row digest, fields, body, and whether a head already carries it), then lifts only on that row digest typed back at a terminal (its first eight hex), or on `--digest <hex>` naming the digest the preview printed. A bare `--yes` names no digest and lifts nothing. A lift signs under the face's root, so a lift always asks the face's passphrase at a terminal; `--digest` spares the typed-back digest alone.

The lift names its taint list: `--taint none` when every input came from inside the face, else `--taint a,b`. A lift carries the staged row's own body and fields, so stage them first (`face.draft.stages`); a lift naming `--text`, `--file` or `--fields` refuses `kahua-lift-unstaged`. `--parent <cid>` names the revision it supersedes (`none` for a first lift), `--sources` further daemon sources the item distils (the staged row always rides), and `--proposal <id>` the proposal it answers: the proposal's body digest must equal the staged body's. Two digests share one word: the ROW digest (what `kahua stage` answers and a lift names) covers the row's body and fields, while a proposal's `digest` names the BODY digest, the body bytes alone.

The door re-reads the row at the act and refuses `kahua-lift-unstaged` (no such row) or `kahua-lift-digest-moved` (the row moved since the preview); a lift the head already carries lands nothing. The lift reads the lōkahi cap off the vessel's island and the operator's grant out of sealed custody, and refuses by name; an AI seat proposes and stages, and its session never lifts. `lares shore lift-kahua` lifts a different thing, the pending set a lay left behind (`carriage.draft.lifts`).

Under a pūlama the root signs at the pūlama's hand door, since the vessel there holds no face root: `--terms` runs every gate and prints ONE stdout line (the one unsigned act its root signs) and opens no route; the pūlama's `sign '<terms>'` checks it and signs; `--land '<answer>'` lands the signed record, where the door builds the act afresh and lands it only over a byte-equal body. Neither asks the passphrase on the vessel, and the host shim walks the pattern (`tools/lares-container.sh kahua lift|withdraw|carry`).

! face.hand.withdraws ~ the hand takes one lifted revision off the stage

`kahua withdraw <cid>` withdraws one lifted revision of the face's stage, an act signed under the face's root out of sealed custody (the lōkahi cap and the operator's grant). It runs on a person's hand alone: an AI seat proposes and stages, and its session never withdraws; no tool carries it. Every answer prints as JSON.

Under a pūlama the root signs at the pūlama's hand door, since the vessel there holds no face root: `--terms` runs every gate and prints ONE stdout line (the one unsigned act its root signs) and opens no route; the pūlama's `sign '<terms>'` checks it and signs; `--land '<answer>'` lands the signed record, where the door builds the act afresh and lands it only over a byte-equal body. Neither asks the passphrase on the vessel, and the host shim walks the pattern (`tools/lares-container.sh kahua lift|withdraw|carry`).

! face.mount.wears ~ unlock opens custody; wear chooses the face

`lares wear N` moves the vessel's mount to face hN, a face already standing open (under a pūlama, one the pūlama lends), and the vessel composes again on it. The door reads the custody door first: a vessel holding no key takes no wear and names the one act that opens it (`lares vault unlock`). A wear asks no route and carries none, so nothing here reaches for a prompt; the face rides the positional, or `--face N`.

A wear that turns the face flushes every shore first, inside the vessel, while the face it leaves still stands mounted, and its answer names one line per island. Where the flush leaves a record unwritten, a person at a terminal answers whether to turn anyway; an agent carries `--yes`. A wear that lands replays the share landing, as an unlock does, and names what moved and what still waits on a shut face. A pipe reads one sentence of prose; `--json` reads the envelope.
