! face.spirit.summons ~ summon ~ the house starts its own arm

`lares spirit summon <pet>#<n> --mandate <uri>@<hash>` reads and verifies the mandate, checks it names this instance and the answering face, reads custody (a hand, or the coordinator's own mandate granting it) and claims a lane on the coordinator's ledger, then lands the summons edge ahead of the launch, so no process stands that the house holds no record of. The host launch cap (`tools/summon-launch.mjs`) starts the process detached; the edge records what it launched holding. A retry that finds the edge naming its launch starts nothing. A launch that started nothing frees its lane; one whose receipt never came keeps it.


THE GUEST'S REACH: a summoned instance arrives as a guest and holds the guest's reach where its mandate names none (the lares doors, Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, and the shell for git, node and pnpm: one table, `GUEST_REACH` in `@lararium/mesh/spirit-summons`); the mandate's hash-covered `--allowed-tools` shapes it, a bare comma-joined list naming the reach exactly (narrowing for a reader) and a list led by `+` widening the guest's reach (for a builder), `mandate-allowed-tools-malformed` otherwise; the edge records the reach as `launched-reach`.

THE SUMMONS FORKS A STREAM: ahead of the launch the instance's stream (`<pet>#<n>`) takes its first entry through the msg door (lar:///engine.msg.lands), its `re` naming the summoner's head (`--stream <pet>#<n>`, else the summoning process's own `LARES_SUMMONED`, else the coordinator the mandate names) and its `about` the mandate at its hash; the edge records `stream`, `summoner-stream` and `forked`, so a retry forks nothing twice, and the launched process carries `LARES_SUMMONED`, the `stream=` default its `lares msg` reads. A hand-back that closes an edge lands one msg on the SUMMONER's stream, `to` the summoner, its `re` the mandate and the instance's last entry, its `about` the hand-back record (`joined` on the edge); a stream write the msg door refuses stops neither act, and the answer names why.

! face.spirit.trues ~ ah ~ one slot replaced or one line added, base-checked

The stack slot `#/has` takes one cap per `--add`. `--instance` names the writer, joins the presence, and refuses during that instance's crossing.

Three other modes ride the verb. `--new` lands a whole shrine from one source. `--offer` lands an offering (ʻālana) on the spirit's shelf before any instance wakes: the mandate words (else the card's own `lane`), `--lane` its memory pointer, `--grant` the grant's slice; a seat names its own `--instance`. `--echo <hash> --instance <id>` lands an instance's echo of the mandate om handed it. Words pass the strict secret-shape guard first.

! library.oracle.speaks ~ a blind throw to collide uncertainty with

The house consults an oracle whose corpus rests on a library shelf (`lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/library/oracles/<kind>/`). The kind rides as data: `by` names the shelf (the E-Jing by default), and the shelf's index record declares its own `method`, its corpus and its credits. The e-jing and doa shelves declare `three-coins`: the I Ching by three coins a line (heads three, tails two: 6 old yin and 9 old yang change, 7 and 8 hold). A new oracle joins as a shelf, never a new address or a new verb; a shelf whose method the verb runs not yet refuses by name.

Every consult lands once, as a meme under `lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/oracle/casts/`, whose five slots run OODA-HA (`#/loop`), whatever the kind. The ask fills `#/observe` with its context pointers and `#/orient` with its gathered uncertainty and its query; the house fills `#/decide` with the throw and every reading the wiki holds, each source credited; the seat appends its reading, its move and its aftermath by slot append. The verb reads the loop's shape from the carrier the caller's stack seats for this address (a carrier a working layer seats above canon shapes the act in its place), the affordance pack its binary baked standing as the floor, and the answer names the carrier slot that shaped it. One asking, one throw: the same query by the same booked asker answers the standing cast and names the uncertainty it kept. The coins draw through the platform's entropy door, or a person types the six values thrown with real coins. The verb reads no clock: the caller names the time as testimony. A weak seed reads back: the record names a seed by a 16-hex digest anyone can test a guess against, so a person choosing one chooses a strong one.

The cast stands as a blind throw to collide uncertainty with: the throw stands, the reading stays open.

The heading `library` names where the consult reads: the oracle shelves rest among the library's holdings, the ones the `lares library` door keeps. The facet `oracle` names the shelf family it reads under, and the dynamic `speaks` names the act: the library's oracle speaks to a fork. No alias stands at an older address (early alpha burns aliases, the operator's word 2026-11-27).

! oracle.calendar.dates ~ the day in the Discordian calendar, from the house's own core

The house computes the day in the Discordian calendar with its own isomorphic core, so a machine with no host `ddate` binary (a vessel's container, a bare host) reads it all the same. Five seasons of 73 days (Chaos, Discord, Confusion, Bureaucracy, The Aftermath) run a five-day week (Sweetmorn, Boomtime, Pungenday, Prickle-Prickle, Setting Orange); the YOLD runs the Gregorian year plus 1166; St. Tib's Day falls on February 29 with no season and no weekday; an apostle's holyday falls on day 5 of a season and its season holyday on day 50.

With no date the verb reads today's local day: the command and the seat each read the clock once, at the caller's side of the seam, and hand the day to the core, which reads none. The `day`, `month` and `year` ride together or not at all (a BCE year rides negative), and a date out of range refuses. X-Day (Confusion 40, 9827 YOLD) stands as the Church of the SubGenius's date, moved forward once the first X-Day passed without incident; `%X` counts the days to it.

Format codes follow ddate(1), with `%E` added: `%A %a` weekday, long and short · `%B %b` season, long and short · `%d` day of the season · `%e` the ordinal (1st, 11th, 21st, 22nd, 23rd) · `%E` the ordinal by its last digit alone (11st, 12nd, 13rd), the first ddate's reading, an easter egg · `%H` the day's holyday, if any · `%N` stop here unless the day holds a holyday · `%Y` the YOLD · `%X` days until X-Day (negative once it passed) · `%n %t` newline, tab · `%.` an exclamation from the platform's entropy door (crypto.getRandomValues) · `%{ %}` the span between them reads "St. Tib's Day" on February 29 and prints plain on every other day.

A bare call answers the default line ("Today is Prickle-Prickle, the 32nd day of The Aftermath in the YOLD 3192"). On a terminal that line prints plain, like ddate(1), and `--json` answers the envelope the seat always returns: {text, entropy, gregorian, yold, tibs, season, dayOfSeason, weekday, holyday}, where `entropy` names the source a `%.` drew from, else null. The verb runs on the host and needs no vessel; the MCP tool rides the @daemon wire.

! realm.bag.shares ~ a bag's share row: names beside names, by reference and never by copy

A share row says who reads and who writes a bag, by face PET-NAME as a title list (`a b [[c d]]`), `*` for every face, or empty; `hN` and `--face N` resolve to that face's pet-name (`--face` adds face N to the readers), so a row always names faces by pet-name. A line names its DELTA: `--read` and `--write` add names beside the standing ones and never replace a list, `--read-remove` and `--write-remove` take names out (each taken-out face's landed grant revokes; a face standing shut keeps the row as it stood, named), and what the line leaves unnamed (the other list, the note, the owner) stands, so the same line twice changes nothing. `--list` shows every row and the one resolver's answer per bag (with `--json`, each row AS WRITTEN beside the resolver's answer); `--remove` unshares the row.

The row writes through to `$LAR_ROOT/config/share.tid` (it survives a re-founding; a person edits it by hand, and the next boot reconciles it in, the file winning) and, with a vessel standing, into the control document (`share-set`); then the operator's hand lands it (`share-apply`): each lit grantee takes the bag's row by reference and a delegation from the owner's hive, and a grant whose face stands shut waits behind an opaque flag until it lights. ONE ROW PER SLUG: a wiki row standing for the slug refuses `share-kind-standing`, and nothing writes. Sharing rides by reference and delegation, never a copy.

! sense.record.flows ~ one verb, N flows: a pet name composes the instruments, never another raw verb

The low-level instruments (crystallize · phase · whiten · couple · gate · mismatch) stand as building blocks a FLOW composes, never the surface: the flow set (crystal · rhythm · couple) carries each pet name, its arity and its cap-stack. A pet name with a `signal` matrix (rows = time, columns = signals; `names` labels the columns) RUNS that flow: the daemon looks its cap-stack up and runs each step routed by hull (crystallize and couple in TypeScript, phase in Python, mismatch in the daemon), threading each outcome to the next. New capability arrives as a new flow.

The CLI reads the signal from an NDJSON file, one JSON array per non-blank line; the seat hands the rows. `target` names the sensorium streams a run reads as provenance: a target with no signal asks the projector to extract one from the target's child streams, which stands feature-gated (the projector runs now, empty until the re-pour lands child signals), so auto-extraction from a poured target stays OWED.

forecast   does a regime shift approach, the R early-warning read (--signal <ndjson>)

!!! aperture ~ the range of the answer

`aperture` takes the set panel's `N/rank` on the seed's own scale (lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/api/noosphere-boot #/aperture): `pulse` 0–4 one has line · `beat` 5–8 the tagline · `measure` 9–12 the card (each slot's first line, a record's text left home) · `arc` 13–16 the whole record (a meme's carrier paged on slot boundaries and joined) · `theme` 17–20 the record and its family. It reads `10/measure`, the rank alone (`measure`) or the number alone (`10`), each resolving to the same band; a rank alone seats its band's canonical number (pulse 2 · beat 6 · measure 10 · arc 16 · theme 18), and the answer echoes the `N/rank` it read. A number and a rank that disagree refuse `aperture-malformed`.

The two dials cross: `aperture=pulse mu=!0` one line asserted · `aperture=measure mu=?0` the card read for relations · `aperture=arc mu=!0` the whole record, every claim checked (a cold read) · `aperture=theme mu=_0` the family's hidden residue. Absent, the door's own default stands: a carrier seats one by its own `aperture` row carrying `default/` (the bare door reads `beat`), and a read with none keeps its gradient.

!!! mu ~ the lens of the answer

A `lares` call and a `set` firing share one param set (lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/api/noosphere-boot #/set-and-setting), so `mu` takes the seed's own TOOL-CARRIES (#/mu-five-tools), character for character: always two hands, the active tool first and the empty hand second. Single tools: `*0` wand (fire, visual feed, ignition) · `?0` cup (water, macro zoom, relation) · `!0` sword (air, micro zoom, certainty) · `_0` pentacle (earth, hidden feed, ground: match without binding). Rest: `00`, the ground state (`arcana` reads it too). Complementary carries across the axes: `*!` detail · `*?` relation · `_!` precision · `_?` overview. Conflict carries on one axis, observable and useful: `*_` signal-jam · `?!` dubious-move; a conflict answers its first tool as written and names the second as the next call, under `mu.next` (the seed's recovery: drop one tool).

A lone glyph, word or value reads pono: `?` reads `?0`, `!` `!0`, `*` `*0`, `_` `_0`, `0` reads `00`; a lone word names its tool or carry; two tools read their canonical carry in either order, while an empty hand written first (`0*`) refuses naming the seed carry: the active hand leads. The glyph stays canonical in sigils and the wiki, the word rides a terminal (a shell globs `*` and `?`, and history-expands `!`). Every answer echoes the full carry it read. Landing 6's words (relate · assert · many · dry · unask) burned: each refuses `mu-malformed` naming its seed carry.

Mu names how a call looks, never how much: the range rides `aperture` (`#/takes/aperture`). The zoom axis runs certainty (sword) against relation (cup), never size.

Each carrier tables the lenses it answers as `cell` rows in its own `#/takes`; a carry outside its table refuses `mu-cell-empty` and names the nearest cell as a call, or the plain call with no `mu`. Rest answers with no cell. The shared row's default reads `00`; a write door seats its own `default/?0` (the receipt's has line).

''The dry band rides the Pentacle's hidden feed.'' A carry holding `_` (`_0`, `_?`, `_!`) walks the door's whole law (every fence, the ocap, the base, the family law) to the last step and lands nothing: `_0` and `_?` answer what the real call would land, the bag and layer, and `needs` (the base it takes); `_!` adds `diff`, each record it would move with its fields before and after and its text line by line. A dry answer carries the carrier's seat hints (`hints`: its `#/gate` rows and any `signs` row). A door that walks no dry path refuses a dry carry `mu-cell-empty` and names the plain call, whatever a layer above tables.

''Fills.'' `fills/observe` takes the ask's context pointers, `fills/uncertain` the ask's gathered uncertainty with its query, `fills/throw` the cast and every reading the wiki holds, each distinct text quoted once with every source's credit beneath it. A slot whose fill the ask left empty, and every slot whose writer reaches the seat, carries its `owes/` ask, marked owed.

The house lands the meme once at the throw; the seat's later writes append to a slot through the one put (`lares put title=<cast> slot='#/decide' append='<words>'`; a slot append needs no base).
